# AntFabric UI

> One component library for AntFabric's web (TanStack Start), desktop (Tauri) and mobile (Expo) apps, written as real components. Two kits take the same props: `@antfabric-ui/react` draws web and desktop, `@antfabric-ui/react-native` draws the phone. 90 components in 12 categories (84 on web, 85 on desktop, 79 on mobile), 90 recipes, 669 design tokens, 17 sample screens.

Paths are relative to the repository root. A path that starts with `/` is on the catalogue site, a static Astro site (`apps/catalogue`) that draws every component live on each platform.

## Packages

- `@antfabric-ui/react`: web and desktop. Peers: `react` and `react-dom` 19.1+, `lucide-react`. Wrap the app in `AntFabricRoot` (`platform`, `os`, `osVersion`, `scheme`, `theme`). With no `theme` it draws `themes.neutral`; AntFabric's own look is `themes.antfabric`.
- `@antfabric-ui/react-native`: the phone. Peers: `react` 19.1+, `react-native` 0.81+, `react-native-svg`, `lucide-react-native`, optionally `expo-glass-effect`. Wrap the app in `ThemeProvider` (`scheme`, `theme`).
- `@antfabric-ui/core`: tokens, recipes, themes (`defineTheme`, `themes`), the stylesheet, the Figtree font files. Both kits depend on it.
- Each kit has three more entries, not part of its root, so an app that never imports one carries none of it: `./data` (KPIs, charts, panels and tables; brings recharts or gifted-charts), `./shell` (the app frame and the pictures of native surfaces: title bars, menus, rails, sidebar, tab bar, OS notification, tray menu, app badge) and `./chat` (the conversation idiom: Message, Composer, ReactionPill, ThreadSummary, TypingIndicator, MessageDivider and, on the web, MessageActions; the agent components stay in the root). Import from `@antfabric-ui/react/data`, `@antfabric-ui/react/shell` or `@antfabric-ui/react/chat`, and the same three names under `@antfabric-ui/react-native`; each component's `platforms.<p>.import` in `/components.json` is its exact line.
- Install, `.npmrc`, fonts, setup and tenant branding: `/install.md` (`CONSUMING.md` in the repository; `/install` on the catalogue is the same guide for a person). How a component is written: `AUTHORING.md`.
- Moving an app from 0.1 to 1.0: `/migrate.md` (`MIGRATION.md` in the repository; `/migrate` on the catalogue is the same guide for a person): the codemod, and every break by area.

## The data

- `/tokens.json` (`packages/core/tokens.json`): the 669 design tokens in the W3C Design Tokens format. Each has `$type`, `$value` (light theme, desktop profile), `$description` (when to use it), and every mode under `$extensions["com.antfabric"].modes` (`{ light, dark }` or `{ web, desktop, mobile }`). A token's path is its name in recipes (`$fg.muted`) and its CSS variable is `--af-fg-muted`. 90 groups: the foundations (`fg`, `surface`, `brand`, `border`, `space`, `radius`, `text`, `font`, `control`, `shadow`, `duration`) and one group per component's own decisions (`button`, `switch`, `dialog`...).
- `/components.json` (`packages/docs/components.json`): all 90 components. Per component: `props` (type, default, the catalogue's sample value where there is one, options, required, platforms, event args and the prop an event changes), `parts`, `recipe` (each part's `$token` references by variant, state and platform), `a11y`, `examples`, `platforms` notes, `related`, and `files`: the paths of both kits, the docs and the recipe.
- `pnpm tokens:build` generates three committed files: `packages/core/tokens.json`, `packages/docs/components.json` and this `llms.txt`. `pnpm check` fails when one is stale. Never edit them by hand; run it after any change to the docs, a recipe or a token.
- `pnpm describe` lists components by category; `pnpm describe <id>` prints one component's props, parts, recipe table, a11y, examples, states, edge cases, matrix, source, flows, related and its four file paths; `pnpm describe tokens` lists the token groups; `pnpm describe tokens <group>` prints each token's path, CSS variable, value per mode, reference and description. Add `--json` to any of them. Run it instead of reading six files.

## Writing a component

1. Two files, one API. Every component is `packages/react/src/components/<category>/<id>.tsx` (web and desktop) and `packages/react-native/src/components/<category>/<id>.tsx` (phone). Both take the props the docs declare for their platforms, plus `style` on the root, and nothing else. Export each from its category's `index.ts`, or from the kit's `src/data/`, `src/shell/` or `src/chat/` entry when it ships from `./data`, `./shell` or `./chat`.
2. The docs file is the contract: `packages/docs/src/components/<category>/<id>.ts` (props, platforms, a11y, examples, edge cases, flows), listed in `packages/docs/src/components/index.ts`. Write it first. Its `level` is `atom` (one control or mark), `molecule` (a few atoms doing one job) or `organism` (a whole region of a screen); a component may import only components at its own level or below, and `pnpm check` holds that. Sample data is AntFabric's own (`#platform-eng`, real names, the AI agent "Fabric"), never lorem ipsum.
3. Styles are a recipe, written once as data: `packages/core/src/recipes/<category>/<id>.ts` with `defineRecipe({ parts, styles })`, added to the category's `index.ts` there. Each part has `base`, `variants` (prop, then value; the docs' `options`), `states` (`hover`, `pressed`, `focus`, `disabled`, `on`, ...), and `platforms` for where the phone differs. Both kits read it through `useRecipe`. The file imports `defineRecipe` from `"../../recipe"` and exports the camelCase of the id (`icon-button` is `iconButton`; a reserved word takes a suffix, `switchRecipe`); the category `index.ts` lists it under the docs id (`"icon-button": iconButton`); a kit reads `import { recipes } from "@antfabric-ui/core"` then `useRecipe(recipes["icon-button"], ...)`. A style that depends on two props together cannot be written (variants layer one prop at a time); `AUTHORING.md`, Recipes, gives the workaround.
4. Tokens only. A recipe value is `"$group.leaf"` (`"$brand.default"`), `"transparent"` or `"none"`; a typo fails `pnpm typecheck`. No hex, no px, no `calc`. A size or colour with no token gets a token first (`packages/core/src/tokens.ts` and `descriptions.ts`), then the recipe reads it. Unitless ratios (`scale: 0.97`) stay in the kit.
5. The kit file keeps behaviour and layout, not style: hover, press and focus, roles, `Animated`, flex direction, `cursor`. It may read `t.space`, `t.duration` and `t.ease`; a style written as `t.something` outside the recipe fails `pnpm check`.
6. Mark every part. Web and desktop: `data-af-part="<part>"` (an `Icon` or `Spinner` takes `part`). Phone: `testID="<id>.<part>"`. A part with no mark fails `pnpm check recipes`. A static component (a divider, a heading) drops `useInteraction` / `usePress`, the handlers, the recipe's `states` and the `state` passed to `useRecipe`, but still marks its parts; for a separator use `role="separator"` on the web, and on the phone (`accessibilityRole` has no separator value) hide a decorative line with `accessibilityElementsHidden` and `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"`.
7. Events are props named `onX`, called with the documented `args` and nothing else: `onClick={() => onPress?.()}`, never `onClick={onPress}`. A prop a press changes (`checked`, `open`, `value`) goes through `useControllable(value, onEvent)`, and the docs declare that event with `changes: "<prop>"`.
8. React kit: states come from `useInteraction()`, never CSS `:hover`; borders are longhands (`borderWidth`, `borderStyle`, `borderColor`), never the `border` shorthand. React Native kit: `usePress()`, no hover; every `Text` takes its type from the recipe (`r.<part>.text`), every `Icon` gets a `color`, fonts by file through `font(weight)`; never `{str && <X />}` with a string or number.
9. Import sibling components from their files (`../actions/button`), never from the kit's index. Icons are lucide names in kebab case. Shortcuts are written `Mod+Enter` and drawn with `formatShortcut(keys, os)`.
10. Accessibility: every icon-only control has a label; the docs' `a11y` says the role and the label.
11. Run `pnpm check <id>` until it passes: it type-checks both kits, checks the docs, the recipe and the props parity, renders every example, variant, state and edge case on every OS, and re-renders through every state. `pnpm check` runs everything. `pnpm frames <id>` shows where flow presses land.
12. Status: a component's own `status` in the docs is `"stable"`, `"beta"` or `"draft"` (a new one is `draft`); each platform's `platforms.<p>.status` is `"ready"`, `"partial"`, `"planned"` or `"not-applicable"` (with an `alternative`).
13. Decisions that are the owner's (a value that differs between the kits, a new token name) go in a GitHub issue, stating what the components do now and naming the component. Do not publish by hand; releases go through the Changesets pipeline (`RELEASING.md`).

## Copy these

Button is the canonical component. Read these four, change what differs:

- docs: `packages/docs/src/components/actions/button.ts`
- recipe: `packages/core/src/recipes/actions/button.ts`
- react kit: `packages/react/src/components/actions/button.tsx`
- react-native kit: `packages/react-native/src/components/actions/button.tsx`

Templates, each a complete `Example` component with its recipe inline as a `defineRecipe` constant and the docs file's shape in a comment:

- `packages/react/TEMPLATE.tsx`
- `packages/react-native/TEMPLATE.tsx`

Their header comments show the recipe file's exact shape, what a static component (no states, no press) drops, and the accessibility roles for a separator or decorative element.

## Adding a component

In this order; `AUTHORING.md` has the same list under "Adding a component: the checklist".

1. Copy both templates to `packages/<kit>/src/components/<category>/<id>.tsx`; rename `Example`; change the `./src/` imports to `../../`.
2. Move the recipe to `packages/core/src/recipes/<category>/<id>.ts` and add its line to that category's `index.ts`.
3. Write `packages/docs/src/components/<category>/<id>.ts` and add its line to `packages/docs/src/components/index.ts`.
4. Export the component and its props type from each kit's category `index.ts` (or from its `./data`, `./shell` or `./chat` entry).
5. `pnpm tokens:build`: regenerates `tokens.json`, `components.json` and `llms.txt`.
6. `pnpm check <id>` until it passes.
7. `pnpm check --update-snapshot`: accepts the new component's render-snapshot keys (`reports/renders.snapshot.json`). Read the diff: only new keys for `<id>`; never use it to hide a change to another component.
8. The full `pnpm check`, green.

## Components

Ids by category. `/components/<id>` is the component's page on the site.

- Actions (Things you press): button, fab, icon-button, segmented-control
- Inputs (Things you type into, pick from or switch): checkbox, chip, form-field, radio-group, search-field, select, switch, text-area, text-field
- Display (People, counts, labels and containers): avatar, avatar-stack, badge, card, divider, kbd, list-item, tag
- Feedback (Progress, loading and the app talking back): empty-state, inline-banner, progress-bar, skeleton, toast, toast-region
- Overlays (Anything that floats above the page): bottom-sheet, command-palette, context-menu, dialog, hover-card, menu, popover, sheet, tooltip
- Navigation (Moving between places inside a screen): breadcrumbs, tabs
- App shell (The frame each platform draws around the product: title bars, menus, rails, tab bars): app-menu-bar, mobile-header, nav-rail, sidebar-item, sidebar-section, tab-bar, title-bar, web-top-bar, workspace-switcher
- Messaging (The conversation surface: messages, threads, the composer): attachment-card, composer, message, message-actions, message-divider, reaction-pill, swipe-row, thread-summary, typing-indicator
- Notifications (How the product reaches someone who isn't looking — on every surface each platform offers): app-badge, in-app-banner, notification-item, notification-schedule, os-notification, permission-prompt, tray-menu
- System states (Offline, updating, signed out, permission denied: the app's own condition): connection-banner, session-state, update-banner
- Human in the loop (An agent working on someone's behalf and stopping to ask: its questions, the approvals it waits for, and what it is doing): agent-steps, approval-item, question-panel, thinking-indicator
- Data (Numbers and the charts and tables that show them: a value and its change, a trend, a chart, a table): bar-chart, breakdown, combo-chart, delta, donut-chart, gauge-chart, goal-rings, kpi-card, line-chart, meter, metric-tabs, metric-value, pagination, period-compare, progress-ring, radar-chart, spark-bars, sparkline, stat-tile, table

Ids by level, smallest first: the order the site's sidebar lists them in. A component imports only components at its own level or below.

- Atoms (One control or mark that does not break down further: a button, a badge, a checkbox): app-badge, avatar, badge, button, card, checkbox, chip, delta, divider, fab, form-field, icon-button, kbd, message-divider, meter, metric-value, progress-bar, progress-ring, reaction-pill, skeleton, spark-bars, sparkline, switch, tag, text-area, text-field, tooltip, typing-indicator
- Molecules (A few atoms doing one job together: a search field, a list item, a menu): agent-steps, approval-item, attachment-card, avatar-stack, breadcrumbs, connection-banner, context-menu, empty-state, hover-card, in-app-banner, inline-banner, kpi-card, list-item, menu, message-actions, notification-item, os-notification, pagination, permission-prompt, popover, radio-group, search-field, segmented-control, select, sidebar-item, stat-tile, swipe-row, tabs, thinking-indicator, thread-summary, toast, toast-region, update-banner
- Organisms (A whole region of a screen, built from molecules and atoms: a dialog, the composer, the nav rail): app-menu-bar, bar-chart, bottom-sheet, breakdown, combo-chart, command-palette, composer, dialog, donut-chart, gauge-chart, goal-rings, line-chart, message, metric-tabs, mobile-header, nav-rail, notification-schedule, period-compare, question-panel, radar-chart, session-state, sheet, sidebar-section, tab-bar, table, title-bar, tray-menu, web-top-bar, workspace-switcher
